label: History
value: Anne was orphaned shortly after birth.
unit: Orphaned shortly after birth, Anne spent her early childhood working for impoverished families before being sent to an asylum. At age eleven, she was mistakenly adopted by Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert of Green Gables in Avonlea, Prince Edward Island. Through her vibrant personality and wild imagination, she won the hearts of her guardians, her bosom friend Diana Barry, and the local community. After excelling at the Queen's Academy and teaching locally in Avonlea following Matthew's death, she attended Redmond College in Kingsport, earning her B.A. and making lifelong friends. During her college years, she published a story, received several marriage proposals, and eventually realized her true feelings for her long-time rival and friend, Gilbert Blythe. After becoming engaged to Gilbert, she accepted a position as principal of Summerside High School, where she lived at Windy Willows for three years, navigating local politics and winning over the formidable Pringle family before leaving to marry Gilbert.

label: History
value: Anthony Pye is a student.
unit: Anthony Pye is one of Anne Shirley's students when she begins teaching at the Avonlea school. Before her tenure, his Uncle Richard tells him that a woman cannot manage a school, prompting Anthony to test Anne's authority from his first day. He deliberately disobeys her and displays a sullen, rebellious attitude to prove his uncle right. Anne struggles to handle him for a long time, as traditional punishments and gentle coaxing fail to break his stubborn resistance. The turning point occurs when Anne finally loses her temper and whips him, an act that unexpectedly earns Anthony's deep respect. From that moment on, Anthony becomes one of her most loyal, obedient, and devoted pupils in Avonlea.

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina enters Anne Shirley's life.
unit: Aunt Jamesina enters Anne Shirley's life when Anne, Priscilla Grant, Stella Maynard, and Philippa Gordon decide to rent Patty's Place in Kingsport while attending Redmond College. Stella arranges for her aunt to live with them as a chaperone, along with Aunt Jamesina's two beloved cats, Joseph and Sarah. She quickly wins the hearts of all four girls with her good humor, delicious cooking, and sensible advice on courtship and life. During their years at Patty's Place, she presides over their cozy domestic life, hosting friends like Gilbert Blythe and Roy Gardner. After the girls graduate and part ways, she continues to maintain a warm friendship with Anne.

She quickly wins the hearts of all four girls with her good humor, delicious cooking, and sensible advice on courtship and life. During their years at Patty's Place, she presides over their cozy domestic life, hosting friends like Gilbert Blythe and Roy Gardner. After the girls graduate and part ways, she continues to maintain a warm friendship with Anne.

label: History
value: Billy Andrews grows up in Avonlea.
unit: Billy Andrews grows up in Avonlea as a neighbor and schoolmate of Anne Shirley. As a young man, he decides he wants to marry Anne, but his extreme shyness prevents him from courting her directly. Instead, he sends his sister, Jane Andrews, to propose to Anne on his behalf. Anne promptly and firmly declines the proposal, which Billy accepts without much heartbreak or distress. He later moves on and marries Nettie Blewett, settling down into a conventional life in Avonlea.

label: History
value: James Boyd is universally known as Captain Jim.
unit: James Boyd, universally known as Captain Jim, spent most of his life as a sailor before retiring to become the keeper of the Four Winds Light on Prince Edward Island. When Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe move to their 'house of dreams' nearby, Captain Jim immediately befriends them, welcoming them into his light-house and sharing his colorful life stories. He introduces Anne to Leslie Moore and takes a deep interest in helping Leslie through her tragic life circumstances. Captain Jim keeps a beloved 'life-book' filled with notes of his maritime adventures, which he long hopes will be published. He entrusts these memoirs to Owen Ford, a visiting author, who turns the Captain's life experiences into a successful novel. Shortly after seeing his life's book completed and witnessing Leslie Moore's newfound happiness, Captain Jim passes away peacefully in his sleep at the lighthouse.

label: History
value: Charlotta the Fourth is hired to manage the housework at Patty's Place in Kingsport.
unit: Charlotta the Fourth is hired to manage the housework at Patty's Place in Kingsport when Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, Philippa Gordon, and Stella Maynard rent the cottage during their college years at Redmond. She arrives eager to carry on the family tradition of her three elder sisters who previously worked for Miss Patty Spofford and Miss Maria Lawson. Throughout Anne's time at Redmond, Charlotta manages the cooking, cleaning, and upkeep of Patty's Place with great devotion and affection for the students. She forms a deep attachment to Anne, whom she idolizes and consults on various personal matters. When the girls graduate and relinquish Patty's Place, Charlotta tearfully returns home, having earned the lasting gratitude and affection of all the cottage's residents.

unit: Charlotta the Fourth is hired to manage the housework at Patty's Place in Kingsport when Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, Philippa Gordon, and Stella Maynard rent the cottage during their college years at Redmond. She arrives eager to carry on the family tradition of her three elder sisters who previously worked for Miss Patty Spofford and Miss Maria Lawson. Throughout Anne's time at Redmond, Charlotta manages the cooking, cleaning, and upkeep of Patty's Place with great devotion and affection for the students. She forms a deep attachment to Anne, whom she idolizes and consults on various personal matters. When the girls graduate and relinquish Patty's Place, Charlotta tearfully returns home, having earned the lasting gratitude and affection of all the cottage's residents.

value: Cornelia is sharp-tongued.

She is a loyal neighbor, a tireless caregiver during illness, and a devoted friend once her trust is earned.

label: History
value: Miss Cornelia Bryant welcomes Anne and Gilbert Blythe
unit: Miss Cornelia Bryant welcomes Anne and Gilbert Blythe when they move into the 'house of dreams' at Four Winds Light. She quickly becomes a frequent visitor, providing Anne with local news, practical advice, and domestic help. Cornelia shows fierce devotion to her neighboring friend Leslie Moore, protecting her interests and offering staunch support. When Anne loses her first child, Joy, Cornelia steps in as a comforting, practical nurse. She later assists Leslie when Dick Moore undergoes brain surgery in Montreal, and she celebrates Leslie's eventual happiness when Dick is revealed to be his cousin George Moore. To the great surprise of her neighbors given her famous anti-marriage sentiments, Cornelia eventually accepts a proposal from her longtime friend Marshall Elliott after he finally shaves his beard following a political victory.

To the great surprise of her neighbors given her famous anti-marriage sentiments, Cornelia eventually accepts a proposal from her longtime friend Marshall Elliott after he finally shaves his beard following a political victory.

label: History
value: Davy's mother dies.
unit: Davy and his twin sister Dora are taken in by Marilla Cuthbert at Green Gables after their mother dies and no other relatives step forward to care for them. While Dora is quiet and perfectly behaved, Davy immediately turns the household upside down with his mischievous pranks, such as locking Dora in a closet or eating all the plum jam. Anne Shirley takes a special interest in raising him, managing his wild behavior with love, patience, and imaginative stories rather than strict discipline. Under Anne's influence, Davy forms a deep attachment to her and tries hard to be a better boy. As he grows older, he continues his schooling in Avonlea while remaining a source of lively humor and warmth at Green Gables.

label: History
value: Diana Barry meets Anne Shirley in Avonlea.
unit: Diana Barry meets Anne Shirley in Avonlea, and the two quickly become inseparable 'bosom friends.' Early in their friendship, Diana's mother temporarily forbids them from seeing each other after Diana accidentally gets drunk on Marilla's raspberry cordial, mistaking it for tea; however, Diana's mother relents after Anne saves Diana's baby sister Minnie May from croup. Diana attends the local school and later Queen's Academy prep classes with Anne, though she opts not to attend Queen's herself, preferring to stay in Avonlea. label: History
value: Dick Moore married Leslie West in Four Winds.
unit: Dick Moore married Leslie West in Four Winds, though the marriage was unhappy and forced by her mother. Shortly after the wedding, Dick joined a sealing ship and vanished, leaving Leslie behind to care for her home and assume he was dead or had abandoned her. Years later, Captain Jim learned of a helpless, memory-lost man matching Dick's description in a Cuban hospital and helped Leslie bring him home. Leslie spent years nursing him faithfully, bound by duty, despite his complete loss of memory and childlike mental state. Later, when Gilbert Blythe arranged for a surgery performed by a specialist, it was revealed through a physical scar that the man was actually Dick's cousin, George Moore, who closely resembled him. Upon learning this, Leslie was freed from her tragic burden, and the true fate of the real Dick Moore—who had died of yellow fever in Cuba years prior—was finally established.

label: History
value: Dora arrives at Green Gables.
unit: Dora arrives at Green Gables alongside her twin brother Davy following the death of their mother. While Davy constantly gets into scrapes and tests Marilla's patience, Dora settles in smoothly, proving to be a model child who never misbehaves. Anne Shirley and Marilla raise the twins together, though Anne often finds Dora's absolute perfection a bit boring compared to Davy's lively antics. As Anne leaves for Redmond College and later takes a teaching position in Summerside, Dora continues to grow up quietly at Green Gables under Marilla's care, maintaining her orderly and dependable nature.

label: History
value: Gilbert first meets Anne Shirley at the Avonlea schoolhouse.
unit: Gilbert first meets Anne Shirley at the Avonlea schoolhouse, where he pulls her red braid and calls her 'Carrots,' prompting her to smash her slate over his head and refuse to speak to him for years. Despite her coldness, Gilbert protects and competes with her academically, eventually giving up his appointment as teacher at the Avonlea school so Anne can stay at Green Gables after Matthew's death. This sacrifice breaks the ice, and they become close friends throughout their teaching years and their time at Redmond College. Gilbert falls deeply in love with Anne and proposes to her during their college years, but she rejects him, leading to a period of painful distance. After graduating from Redmond with highest honors, Gilbert contracts typhoid fever, bringing Anne to the realization of her true feelings for him. Upon recovering, he proposes again, and Anne accepts. While Anne works as a principal in Summerside, Gilbert completes his medical degree at Bellevue Hospital in New York and arranges to take over a practice in Glen St. Mary.

During his time living as a bachelor in Avonlea, Mr. Harrison becomes a well-known, if eccentric, figure among the local neighbors. His domestic life changes dramatically when his estranged wife, Emily, unexpectedly arrives in Avonlea, leading to their reconciliation and her taking up residence with him on the farm.

label: History
value: Josie Pye grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Josie Pye grew up in Avonlea and attended the local school, where she frequently clashed in spirit with Anne Shirley and her circle of friends. During a game of dare at Diana Barry's party, she dared Anne to walk the ridge-pole of the Barry roof, which resulted in Anne falling and breaking her ankle. Later, Josie joined the Queen's class and studied to become a teacher alongside Anne, Gilbert Blythe, and Jane Andrews. After passing her exams and obtaining her teaching license, she went on to teach at various island schools. Throughout her school years and young adulthood, she remained a consistent source of catty remarks and social friction within the Avonlea youth cohort.

label: History
value: Lavendar Lewis lived a quiet, secluded life.
unit: Miss Lavendar Lewis lived a quiet, secluded life at Echo Lodge in Grafton after a youthful quarrel separated her from her fiancé, Stephen Irving. To cope with her loneliness, she created a fantasy world of imaginary company and dressed in lovely lavender gowns. Anne Shirley met her while selling subscriptions for the Avonsea Improvement Society and the two immediately bonded as kindred spirits. Anne brought Stephen's son, Paul Irving, to visit, which rekindled memories of her lost love. Upon learning that Stephen had returned from the United States, Anne helped facilitate their reunion. Stephen and Miss Lavendar reconciled their past misunderstandings and were married in a joyful ceremony at Echo Lodge, after which they moved to Boston with Paul.

label: History
value: Leslie Moore lived a tragic life
unit: Leslie Moore lived a tragic, isolated life at Four Winds until Anne Shirley moved to the house of dreams after marrying Gilbert Blythe. Anne and Leslie gradually formed a close, deep friendship, though Leslie initially struggled with bitterness over Anne's joy compared to her own suffering. When writer Owen Ford visited Four Winds, he used Leslie's life story and her grandfather's journal to write a successful novel, and he and Leslie fell secretly in love. Gilbert Blythe suggested a surgery for Leslie's invalid husband Dick, which revealed after his recovery that he was actually Dick's cousin, George Warren. Freed from her tragic marriage and her years of burdensome caretaking, Leslie pursued nursing training in Montreal. She ultimately accepted Owen Ford's proposal, finally finding the joy and romance that had been denied to her in her youth.

label: History
value: Marilla lives at Green Gables
unit: Marilla lives at Green Gables with her unmarried brother Matthew. Intending to adopt an orphan boy to help on the farm, they are inadvertently sent an imaginative orphan girl named Anne Shirley. Although Marilla initially intends to return Anne, she ultimately agrees to keep her and undertakes her raising with strict discipline that gradually turns into deep love. Following Matthew's sudden death from heart failure, Marilla faces severe eye strain and the threat of blindness, which leads her to consider selling Green Gables; however, Anne foregoes her college scholarship to remain in Avonlea as a schoolteacher, allowing them to stay in their home. Later, Marilla takes in her late second cousin Mary Keith's twin children, Davy and Dora, whose upbringing challenges and softens her further. Throughout Anne's college years and her subsequent teaching tenure in Summerside, Marilla remains the steady emotional heart of Green Gables, eagerly anticipating Anne's letters and visits.

label: History
value: Marshall Elliott is a long-time resident of Four Winds.
unit: Marshall Elliott is a long-time resident of Four Winds who made a famous political vow in his youth never to shave or cut his hair until the Liberals won the election. Because the Conservatives remained in power for decades, Marshall's hair and beard grew to extraordinary lengths, making him one of the coastline's notable eccentrics. He held a long-standing affection for Miss Cornelia Bryant, but she refused to marry a man who looked like a tramp. When the Liberals finally won a general election, Marshall promptly went to the barber, cut his hair, shaved his beard, and bought a new suit of clothes. Transformed back into a handsome, respectable man, he immediately proposed to Miss Cornelia Bryant. She accepted him, and the two were happily married, settling down together in Four Winds.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert lives at Green Gables
unit: Matthew Cuthbert lives at Green Gables with his unmarried sister, Marilla. Aging and suffering from a failing heart, Matthew agrees with Marilla to adopt an orphan boy to help with farm work. When Matthew goes to the Bright River station, he finds Anne Shirley instead, whom he immediately grows fond of on the ride home. He gently convinces Marilla to keep Anne, and over the following years, he acts as Anne's sympathetic champion and indulgent father figure. When Anne wants a puffed-sleeve dress for a Christmas concert, Matthew braves his terror of shopwomen to purchase the materials for her. He takes quiet pride in Anne's academic triumphs as she attends Queen's Academy and earns a scholarship to Redmond College. Shortly after Anne completes her studies at Queen's, the Abbey Bank fails, wiping out the Cuthberts' savings; upon reading the news, Matthew suffers a fatal heart attack and dies instantly. His memory continues to deeply inspire and comfort Anne as she goes on to teach and later attend college.

unit: Matthew Cuthbert lives at Green Gables with his unmarried sister, Marilla. Aging and suffering from a failing heart, Matthew agrees with Marilla to adopt an orphan boy to help with farm work. When Matthew goes to the Bright River station, he finds Anne Shirley instead, whom he immediately grows fond of on the ride home. He gently convinces Marilla to keep Anne, and over the following years, he acts as Anne's sympathetic champion and indulgent father figure. When Anne wants a puffed-sleeve dress for a Christmas concert, Matthew braves his terror of shopwomen to purchase the materials for her. He takes quiet pride in Anne's academic triumphs as she attends Queen's Academy and earns a scholarship to Redmond College. Shortly after Anne completes her studies at Queen's, the Abbey Bank fails, wiping out the Cuthberts' savings; upon reading the news, Matthew suffers a fatal heart attack and dies instantly. His memory continues to deeply inspire and comfort Anne as she goes on to teach and later attend college.

label: History
value: Owen Ford travels to Four Winds Light.
unit: Owen Ford travels to Four Winds Light on Prince Edward Island to recover from illness and seek inspiration for his writing, boarding with Captain Jim. While there, he meets Anne Shirley and Leslie Moore, becoming deeply enchanted by Leslie despite her tragic circumstances and marriage to the brain-injured Dick Moore. Owen learns of Captain Jim's life experiences and recognizes the potential for a great novel, purchasing the old captain's 'life-book' to adapt it into prose. He writes the masterpiece The Life-Book of Captain Jim while staying at Four Winds and falls hopelessly in love with Leslie. After the book is completed and accepted for publication, he leaves Four Winds, unable to press his feelings upon the married Leslie. Later, when it is discovered that Dick Moore is actually his cousin George Moore and Dick himself had died years prior, Leslie is freed from her tragic marriage. Owen returns to Four Winds after his book becomes a literary triumph, proposes to Leslie, and the two are married at Anne's house before departing to start their new life together in America.

While there, he meets Anne Shirley and Leslie Moore, becoming deeply enchanted by Leslie despite her tragic circumstances and marriage to the brain-injured Dick Moore. Owen learns of Captain Jim's life experiences and recognizes the potential for a great novel, purchasing the old captain's 'life-book' to adapt it into prose. He writes the masterpiece The Life-Book of Captain Jim while staying at Four Winds and falls hopelessly in love with Leslie. After the book is completed and accepted for publication, he leaves Four Winds, unable to press his feelings upon the married Leslie. Later, when it is discovered that Dick Moore is actually his cousin George Moore and Dick himself had died years prior, Leslie is freed from her tragic marriage. Owen returns to Four Winds after his book becomes a literary triumph, proposes to Leslie, and the two are married at Anne's house before departing to start their new life together in America.

label: History
value: Paul Irving arrives in Avonlea
unit: Paul Irving arrives in Avonlea as a young boy to live with his grandmother and attend the Avonlea school. Anne Shirley, taking up her first teaching position, quickly recognizes Paul as a 'kindred spirit' due to his vivid imagination and creative mind. Paul invents an intricate cast of imaginary companions, including 'rock people,' and shares his private stories with Anne. When his father, Stephen Irving, visits Avonlea, Paul unwittingly helps bridge the long-standing rift between Stephen and his old sweetheart, Miss Lavendar Lewis. Anne brings Stephen to Miss Lavendar's cottage at Echo Lodge, leading to their reconciliation and marriage. Following the wedding, Paul leaves Avonlea to live with his father and stepmother, though he maintains a loving correspondence with Anne as he continues his education and matures into a talented young man.

unit: Paul Irving arrives in Avonlea as a young boy to live with his grandmother and attend the Avonlea school. Anne Shirley, taking up her first teaching position, quickly recognizes Paul as a 'kindred spirit' due to his vivid imagination and creative mind. Paul invents an intricate cast of imaginary companions, including 'rock people,' and shares his private stories with Anne. When his father, Stephen Irving, visits Avonlea, Paul unwittingly helps bridge the long-standing rift between Stephen and his old sweetheart, Miss Lavendar Lewis. Anne brings Stephen to Miss Lavendar's cottage at Echo Lodge, leading to their reconciliation and marriage. Following the wedding, Paul leaves Avonlea to live with his father and stepmother, though he maintains a loving correspondence with Anne as he continues his education and matures into a talented young man.

label: History
value: Philippa meets Anne Shirley at Redmond College in Kingsport.
unit: Philippa meets Anne Shirley at Redmond College in Kingsport, where they quickly become close friends. She joins Anne, Priscilla Grant, and Stella Maynard in renting Patty's Place, a cozy cottage where they live during their college years. Although pursued by numerous wealthy suitors, including her long-time admirers Alec and Alonso, Philippa ultimately falls in love with Jonas Blake, a poor divinity student. Recognizing that true devotion and character matter more than wealth, she accepts Jonas's proposal and joyfully adapts to the prospect of life as a minister's wife. After graduating from Redmond College, she marries Jonas and moves away to support his ministry, remaining a devoted friend and correspondent to Anne.

unit: Philippa meets Anne Shirley at Redmond College in Kingsport, where they quickly become close friends. She joins Anne, Priscilla Grant, and Stella Maynard in renting Patty's Place, a cozy cottage where they live during their college years. Although pursued by numerous wealthy suitors, including her long-time admirers Alec and Alonso, Philippa ultimately falls in love with Jonas Blake, a poor divinity student. Recognizing that true devotion and character matter more than wealth, she accepts Jonas's proposal and joyfully adapts to the prospect of life as a minister's wife. After graduating from Redmond College, she marries Jonas and moves away to support his ministry, remaining a devoted friend and correspondent to Anne.

label: History
value: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolteacher in Avonlea
unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolteacher in Avonlea during Anne Shirley's early years at Green Gables. During his tenure, he openly courted one of his older pupils, Prissy Andrews, causing much gossip in the community and leading him to neglect the rest of the school. He antagonized Anne Shirley on several occasions, notably misspelling her name on the blackboard, punishing her for being late by forcing her to sit next to Gilbert Blythe, and humiliating her for losing her temper. These incidents prompted Anne to refuse to attend school for a time. Later, he organized a test class for pupils preparing for the Queen's Academy entrance examinations, which included Anne and Gilbert. At the end of the school year, he gave a surprisingly emotional farewell speech before leaving Avonlea permanently.

He antagonized Anne Shirley on several occasions, notably misspelling her name on the blackboard, punishing her for being late by forcing her to sit next to Gilbert Blythe, and humiliating her for losing her temper. These incidents prompted Anne to refuse to attend school for a time. Later, he organized a test class for pupils preparing for the Queen's Academy entrance examinations, which included Anne and Gilbert. At the end of the school year, he gave a surprisingly emotional farewell speech before leaving Avonlea permanently.

label: History
value: Roy Gardner meets Anne Shirley at Redmond College.

He courts Anne persistently throughout their college years, showering her with flowers, poetry, and devotion. Anne accepts his courtship, believing him to be her ideal dark, romantic prince. However, over time, Anne's friends and Anne herself subtly realize that despite his good looks and charm, Roy lacks humor and a deeper connection with her. In their senior year, Roy proposes to Anne in a carefully arranged, romantic setting. Anne suddenly realizes she does not love him and rejects his proposal, leaving Roy heartbroken and ending their relationship.

label: History
value: Ruby Gillis grows up in Avonlea.
unit: Ruby Gillis grows up in Avonlea as one of Anne Shirley's primary classmates and members of her inner circle of girl friends. During their school years, she joins the Story Club, though her contributions lean heavily toward sensational romance. After attending Queen's Academy to earn a teaching license alongside Anne and the rest of the Avonlea cohort, Ruby takes up teaching positions at local schools, including Carmody and White Sands. Throughout her youth and early adulthood, she actively collects a succession of suitors and beaux, frequently bragging about her romantic conquests to her friends. While Anne pursues higher education at Redmond College, Ruby remains in PEI, continuing her social life and teaching, always preoccupied with the local marriage market.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy comes to Avonlea
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy comes to Avonlea to take over the local school following the departure of Mr. Phillips. She quickly revolutionizes the classroom by introducing modern teaching techniques, nature walks, physical culture, and literary recitations. She forms a special bond with Anne Shirley and establishes an advanced 'Queen's Class' to coach bright students for the entrance examinations to Queen's Academy. Through her diligent instruction and encouragement, all of her candidates pass the exams with high honors. After her successful tenure in Avonlea, she moves on to accept a teaching position at a high school in Middlebridge.

She forms a special bond with Anne Shirley and establishes an advanced 'Queen's Class' to coach bright students for the entrance examinations to Queen's Academy. Through her diligent instruction and encouragement, all of her candidates pass the exams with high honors. After her successful tenure in Avonlea, she moves on to accept a teaching position at a high school in Middlebridge.

label: History
value: Stella Maynard first meets Anne Shirley
unit: Stella Maynard first meets Anne Shirley while attending Queen's Academy in Charlottetown, where both study to earn their teaching certificates. After teaching for a time, Stella decides to pursue a Bachelor of Arts degree at Redmond College in Kingsport, joining Anne, Priscilla Grant, and Philippa Gordon. To make their college years more comfortable, Stella proposes renting a cozy house called Patty's Place and brings her beloved Aunt Jamesina to keep house for them. The four girls enjoy a delightful and memorable two years living together at Patty's Place until their graduation. After graduating from Redmond, Stella accepts a teaching position.

label: History
value: Susan Baker enters the series when Gilbert and Anne Blythe move to their first home.
unit: Susan Baker enters the series when Gilbert and Anne Blythe move to their first home, the House of Dreams in Four Winds, and hire her as their resident housekeeper. She quickly becomes an indispensable part of the household, helping Anne manage the home and offering steadfast support through emotional hardships, including the loss of Anne's first child, Joy. When the Blythes move to a larger home at Ingleside in Glen St. Mary, Susan moves with them and continues her dedicated service. Over the years, she plays a major role in raising the growing Blythe family—Jem, Walter, the twins Nan and Di, Shirley, and Rilla—loving each child as if they were her own. During Anne's temporary absence in Summerside prior to their move to Ingleside, and throughout the years at Ingleside, Susan remains the backbone of domestic life at the doctor's house.
